items.summary: The global AI data centre boom is creating fresh opportunities for power and cooling equipment suppliers as developers race to overcome infrastructure bottlenecks. Rising demand for transformers, efficient power systems and liquid cooling is benefiting companies across Asia, although high valuations, supply constraints, competition and deployment delays remain key risks for investors.

items.summary: Tim Cook leaves Apple after 15 years with India as a key part of his supply-chain legacy. What began with assembling older iPhones in 2017 has grown into a major global manufacturing hub, with India now making about one in four iPhones and potentially expanding into MacBooks and iPads.

items.title: ONGC Videsh eyes Venezuela oil assets after US green light
items.summary: An Indian investment team is reviewing Venezuelan oil assets after receiving US government approval. This visit marks the first such trip in several years for the company. The team plans to see oil fields and meet with Venezuelan energy officials. They are keen to become operators of existing oil projects and enhance production. This development occurs as Venezuela's oil sales to India are recovering.

items.title: Small finance banks' asset quality to improve, GNPA to fall by March 2027: Crisil Ratings
items.summary: Small finance banks anticipate improved asset quality by March 2027. Gross non-performing assets are projected to decline significantly from current levels. This improvement stems from microfinance portfolio recovery and non-microfinance growth. Tighter underwriting practices have strengthened borrower selection in microfinance portfolios. The non-microfinance segment now forms a larger share of total advances.

items.title: India needs to build advanced tech capabilities, reduce import dependence: Hyundai CEO Tarun Garg
items.summary: Hyundai Motor India MD and CEO Tarun Garg urged India to develop advanced technology capabilities. He stated the nation must move beyond manufacturing scale and reduce import dependence. India's automotive industry has shown resilience and needs to focus on global leadership. The focus should shift from "Make in India" to "Design and Engineer in India". This will help build domestic technology and intellectual property for future growth.

items.title: Won't chase top-line growth at any cost: SBI General CEO on fire insurance pricing war
items.summary: SBI General Insurance will not chase fire insurance business at unsustainable prices. The company aims to improve profitability and maintain a healthy expense of management ratio. Health insurance penetration is a key focus, leveraging SBI's extensive branch network. Addressing mis-selling requires suitability, transparency, convenience, and fairness for customers. SBI General Insurance is considering a potential public listing in the future.

items.title: Warren Buffett once called bonds a terrible investment but later massively invested in them. Here's why
items.summary: Warren Buffett has long warned against long-term bonds, calling them a poor investment for investors with extended horizons. Yet Berkshire Hathaway has amassed a huge short-term Treasury position, highlighting the distinction between long-duration bonds and cash-like instruments. As global yields surge, Buffett’s bond strategy offers a timely lesson for investors.

items.title: Why are global bond yields surging to multi-decade highs?
items.summary: Global government borrowing costs are reaching multi-decade highs as inflation persists. Bond yields in major economies like the United States and Japan have sharply increased. Renewed oil price gains and substantial government debt add to market pressures. Higher borrowing costs impact households, businesses, and government finances significantly. Investors watch for fiscal policy changes and economic growth to stabilize markets.

items.title: TV channel exits accelerate as India’s linear television model comes under pressure
items.summary: India’s television broadcasting industry is undergoing a structural reset as 114 channel licences were surrendered between 2022 and 2026 amid weakening advertising, declining pay-TV homes and audiences shifting to OTT, connected TV and short-form video. Broadcasters including JioStar, Zee Entertainment, NDTV and B4U Networks are rationalising portfolios as industry economics come under pressure.
